title: backfill BFS has no entry-count limit — OOM via adversarial peer
description:
## Why this issue exists

In crates/core/src/group_log/backfill.rs, the backfill() function fetches log entries from a remote peer using a BFS loop. There is no bound on the total number of entries fetched — the loop terminates only when the BFS frontier is empty or every visited entry already exists locally.

An adversarial (or buggy) peer can serve a DAG with millions of entries. Each entry is held in memory as a LogEntry (Vec of parent CIDs), plus the BFS frontier queue, producing unbounded heap growth. There is no timeout and no entry-count circuit-breaker.

## What breaks

A single malicious peer can exhaust process heap and crash stoa-transit. Because backfill is triggered on peering, this is reachable from the network without authentication.

## Fix direction

Add a MAX_BACKFILL_ENTRIES constant (e.g. 50000, same order as MAX_BFS_VISITS in reconcile.rs) and return a partial-backfill error when the limit is hit. Reconcile already has MAX_BFS_VISITS=5000; backfill should match that discipline.
